title: KV eviction storm and multi‑tenancy GPU OOM triage
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and a Private on‑prem deployment observed sudden GPU OOMs during long-lived chat sessions. Root symptoms: large prefix growth on a subset of tenants, unexpected KV cache churn that ramped eviction pressure and produced highly fragmented arenas in the allocator. This ticket coordinates triage, a runtime fix, targeted rollouts, and a postmortem for a regression introduced by the kernel scheduling change in runtime-2026.02. The incident manifests as: (1) high per-session KV allocations that are not reclaimed, (2) eviction storms that cause many small free fragments rather than contiguous free memory, and (3) allocator failing to coalesce resulting in OOMs despite overall free memory. Impact is multi-tenant: hosted customers saw increased 429s and tail latency, dedicated pools hit capacity drains, and an enterprise Private deployment experienced an orchestrator-level node restart due to stuck page faults.
impact:
- Multiple customers degraded: elevated 429/503 rates and token throttling
- Two Dedicated clusters saturated, triggering emergency scaledown and degraded throughput
- One Private on‑prem customer experienced a node restart and required manual remediation
- Estimated downtime window: 2026-03-09T22:00Z -> rolling mitigations applied by 2026-03-11
- Business: several SRE escalations and SOC engagement for private customer
reproduction_steps: 1) Start long-lived chat sessions that accumulate prefixes (>=20k tokens aggregated across turns) on hosted/dedicated/private runtime-2026.02 builds
2) Simulate mixed workload: many small queries + a small portion (~5%) of long-context streaming sessions
3) Observe KV handle growth via /metrics (kvcache_handles_total, kvcache_evictions_total) and per-session allocation traces
4) Monitor allocator fragmentation via debug histogram endpoints (arena_free_fragmentation_pct, slab_count) and GPU memory usage per process
5) Reproduce OOM within 10–30 minutes on medium-size GPU nodes under load when eviction rate > 5000/min
investigation: Initial triage (2026-03-09): correlation between commit c3a9f2 (kernel-sched heuristics) and first customer reports
Heap snapshots show many small free spans (4–32 KiB) — coalescer not running during aggressive eviction bursts
KV cache metadata contained stale tombstones preventing immediate reuse of slots; concurrent resync was deferred under high contention
Private on‑prem logs show an interaction with older CUDA driver (11.5) where a page fault during eviction delayed compaction timers
Telemetry spike: kvcache_eviction_latency P99 increased from 8ms to 450ms during incidents, allocator_coalesce_timeouts rose sharply
Hypothesis: kernel-sched change increased eviction parallelism which exposed a race between evictor and allocator coalescer leading to fragmentation and leaked KV handles
mitigation: Short term (applied 2026-03-10): throttle KV evictor parallelism to 2 workers for hosted and dedicated to reduce fragmentation bursts
Short term (private customer): patched node with backported driver guard (hotpatch) and disabled aggressive kernel-sched path; provided manual GC script to force KV tombstone compaction
Immediate customer communication: notified impacted accounts and offered 24x7 runbook assistance and credits
Medium term: rolling revert of kernel-sched heuristics in runtime-2026.02 to runtime-2026.02.1 on hosted pools while we validate correctness
rollout_plan: Canary (3% host pool): deploy runtime-2026.02.2 with coalescer watchdog and conservative evictor settings (2026-03-12)
If no regression in 24h: expand to 25% and monitor metrics (kvcache_evictions_total, allocator_free_frag_pct, gpu_mem_free)
Full rollout across hosted and dedicated in 72 hours if metrics stable
Private: provide patch bundle and deterministic test harness for customer to validate before applying same runtime-2026.02.2
Fallback: automated rollback if RSS OOMs > 3/min or P99 latency increases > 25% compared to baseline
monitoring: Dashboards updated: eviction_pressure, evictor_parallelism, allocator_coalesce_failures; alert thresholds: eviction_pressure > 4000/min and coalesce_failures_rate > 0.1/min
Add ephemeral trace tag 'kvcache-evict-race' on suspected sessions to capture stack traces
SLOs to observe during rollout: hosted P99 latency and 429 rate, dedicated throughput, private node restart rate
Background job to sweep stale tombstones faster for first 48h after rollout to accelerate healing
postmortem_actions: 1) Implement deterministic unit/integration tests that simulate eviction bursts and verify allocator coalescing under contention
2) Add a coalescer watchdog that forces a synchronous compaction if free span fragmentation exceeds threshold
3) Harden KV tombstone lifecycle: strong consistency path for tombstone removal when evictor is paused
4) Update driver compatibility matrix and add automated smoke tests covering older CUDA drivers for Private installs
5) Document runbook: how to force-safe-compact, apply hotpatch, and collect heap snapshots for customer SREs
6) Post-release review with product and support to update SLA credits and customer communication templates
